lamaison.name: La Maison Fleurie
lamaison.tags: fine dining • french restaurant • limassol • CMS • web

overview.title: A little piece of Paris, kept alive since 1986.
overview.body: La Maison Fleurie is a family-run French restaurant in Limassol. Since 1986 the Ioannou family has welcomed guests as their own — candlelit room, summer garden, and a menu that travels between Paris and the Mediterranean.

sections.title: Four decades of hospitality.
sections.body: Founded in 1986 by Christos and Eleni Ioannou after a decade in Paris, the restaurant has become a neighbourhood landmark. Recipes from France, warmth from Cyprus.

sections.title: Seasoned by travel.
sections.body: Fresh seafood arrives twice a week, delicacies are imported monthly from France, and the day ends with crème brûlée under candlelight — or in the summer garden.

sections.title: A site as warm as the room.
sections.body: A public website with the menu, gallery, and story — plus a quiet CMS where the team edits dishes, translations, and media without touching code.

agios.name: Taverna Agios Epiktitos
agios.tags: taverna • cypriot cuisine • menu • booking • web

overview.title: From the hills of Armenochori.
overview.body: A family Cypriot taverna in a restored old village school. Here tradition meets hospitality: meat over carob charcoal, bread from the wood-fired oven, and a table that always has room for one more.

sections.title: A restored school, a living table.
sections.body: The taverna lives in a former village school in Armenochori. The building has a new chapter, but the spirit stays the same — gathering, sharing, celebrating.

sections.title: Fire, spice, tradition.
sections.body: From souvlaki to resi, the menu is a tour of Cyprus: slow-cooked meats, aromatic meze, and homemade sweets the way families have made them for generations.

sections.title: A menu, a table, a story.
sections.body: The site carries the full menu with categories, table reservations, and events — and every booking lands straight in the owners' Telegram.

nicks_coffee_bike.name: Nick's Coffee Bike
nicks_coffee_bike.tags: coffee • street corner • coming soon • web

overview.title: Good coffee, on the move.
overview.body: Nick's Coffee Bike is a small coffee cart on wheels — espresso for the street, brewed where people walk by. The site is still in the works, and the idea is simple: good coffee, served warm, wherever Nick parks.

sections.title: Coffee that travels.
sections.body: A bicycle, a cart, and a proper little bar. No queues, no waiting rooms — coffee shows up on the corner, and leaves when it's time to ride.

sections.title: A small cart, a real bar.
sections.body: The gear is serious and the recipe is personal. The kind of coffee you cross the street for, then come back for tomorrow.

sections.title: In the works.
sections.body: The website is being prepared — menu, location, and stories are coming. For now, the best way to find the bike is to follow it on Instagram.

overview.title: Mountains. Lake. Hospitality.
overview.body: Karagat is a mountain hotel — a tall building by the peaks, a conference space beside it, and a kitchen that feeds the morning. Simple, warm, and made for guests.

sections.title: Rooms over the mountains.
sections.body: Comfortable rooms, quiet mornings, and calm lake views a short drive away. The hotel is a base for the mountains and a rest stop after the road.

sections.title: A conference space beside it.
sections.body: An attached conference hall turns the hotel into a place for meetings, workshops, and events — work and rest under one roof.

sections.title: No menu, just home.
sections.body: The kitchen works without a menu — it feeds the morning and cooks what the day brings, the way home cooking works best.

sections.title: A site that books the stay.
sections.body: Rooms, gallery, location, and booking in one calm place. The site shows the view and lets guests reserve without a single extra step.

leondiana.name: Leondiana
leondiana.tags: boutique hotel • larnaca • booking • admin panel • web

overview.title: A quiet corner of Larnaca, distilled into pixels.
overview.body: Leondiana is a boutique hotel in Larnaca, Cyprus — a quiet lane, Mediterranean light, coffee on the balcony, and the sound of the sea. Without the extra noise.

sections.title: A stay that books itself.
sections.body: The guest side is a calm visual journey: a home that carries the atmosphere, four room categories — Standard, Deluxe, Suite, Family — a filterable gallery with lightbox, location, and a booking form that computes the final check on the fly.

sections.title: A quiet command center.
sections.body: Behind the aesthetics sits a functional admin panel: rooms, incoming bookings with statuses, flexible promo codes, two-language content editing, settings, and a media library that places photos into slots without duplication.

sections.title: One source, every surface.
sections.body: The product is split into a user-facing frontend and a data-driven backend (Django + PostgreSQL). A single structured media source feeds the homepage carousel, the general gallery, and a specific room card alike — no duplicates, one truth.

oryzo_ai.name: Daerdree Bar & Timeclub
oryzo_ai.tags: entertainment • lounge concept • booking • UI/UX • web

overview.title: A lounge that sells atmosphere, not drinks.
overview.body: Daerdree Bar & Timeclub needed a digital identity as magnetic as its rooms — an entertainment platform where booking feels like an invitation, not a transaction.

sections.title: Darker, warmer, louder.
sections.body: We leaned into a dusk-toned palette, oversized editorial type, and motion that breathes like nightlife — every screen designed around the pulse of the venue.

sections.title: Reservations without friction.
sections.body: Table selection, date pickers, and time slots were compressed into a single flowing flow, cutting booking time to under a minute.

sections.title: UI that knows your table.
sections.body: Interactive menus, event schedules, and private-club details live in one coherent system — sharp on desktop, equally confident on mobile.

of_the_oak.name: Dastorkon Ethno-Restaurant
of_the_oak.tags: gastronomy • restaurant • interactive menu • i18n • web

overview.title: Heritage plated in pixels.
overview.body: Dastorkon blends centuries of nomad cuisine with a modern dining room. The site had to taste as rich as the menu — and speak fluently in two languages.

sections.title: Every dish has a chapter.
sections.body: We structured the menu as a journey — ingredients, origins, and rituals behind each plate — turning a restaurant site into a cultural archive.

sections.title: A menu that serves itself.
sections.body: Category navigation, dietary filters, and dish photography flow into a calm reading experience, built for both the curious guest and the quick browser.

sections.title: Two tongues, one table.
sections.body: Full i18n between English and Russian — routing, content, and formatting — so every guest reads the story the way it was meant to be told.

overview.title: Complex capital, composed.
overview.body: Walmgres needed an investment platform that makes sophisticated portfolios feel calm, legible, and decision-ready — without drowning in dashboards.

sections.title: Confidence through clarity.
sections.body: A restrained dark interface with precise data hierarchy — numbers lead, decoration follows. Every screen answers: where do I stand?

sections.title: Data that performs.
sections.body: Portfolio breakdowns, performance curves, and risk indicators render as focused charts — engineered to stay instant on heavy datasets.

sections.title: Movement with intent.
sections.body: Transitions between states guide the eye, never distract it. GSAP-driven reveals make navigation feel like an instrument, not a slideshow.

overview.title: A studio that ships velocity.
overview.body: IkSoft is a software studio that builds fast and thinks faster. The showcase had to feel engineered — speed, precision, and a touch of obsession.

sections.title: Performance as identity.
sections.body: We opened with motion and momentum — 3D-led hero, rapid scroll choreography — so the site itself demonstrates what the studio sells.

sections.title: Case studies as products.
sections.body: Project presentations are structured like product pages: problem, process, result. Clients scroll through proof, not promises.

sections.title: Details that compound.
sections.body: Typographic contrast, precise spacing, and micro-interactions tuned by hand — the invisible ingredients of a premium software brand.

synthetic_human.name: Webdoc.life AI
synthetic_human.tags: healthtech • AI medical parser • SaaS • Next.js

overview.title: AI that reads the chart.
overview.body: Webdoc.life parses medical documents into structured health records. The product had to earn trust — clarity and calm were non-negotiable.

sections.title: From paperwork to signal.
sections.body: Upload a document, receive a structured profile. We designed the pipeline so users always see what the AI extracted and why.

sections.title: Transparency by design.
sections.body: Source highlighting and extraction confidence make the machine legible — the interface proves its own accuracy as you watch.

sections.title: Healing, quietly.
sections.body: A light, clinical palette with generous whitespace keeps the experience gentle — technology that steps back so the patient steps forward.

spatial_fusion.name: Careyourpet (PetVet)
spatial_fusion.tags: vet CRM • SaaS • PostgreSQL • web • mobile

overview.title: Every paw, tracked.
overview.body: Careyourpet is a veterinary CRM built for clinics that juggle patients, appointments, and records. The system had to be warm enough for nurses, fast enough for doctors.

sections.title: One record, every visit.
sections.body: A unified patient timeline consolidates medical history, prescriptions, and vaccination schedules — no more paper stacks behind the desk.

sections.title: Built for busy hands.
sections.body: Keyboard-first scheduling, quick-search across pets and owners, and mobile-ready screens keep the whole clinic in the flow.

sections.title: Clinical, not cold.
sections.body: A soft palette and rounded geometry keep the tool approachable — software that respects the people caring for our animals.

spaace.name: Proffmusic.shop
spaace.tags: audio stock • music marketplace • e-commerce • digital assets

overview.title: Sound, sorted.
overview.body: Proffmusic is a marketplace for professional audio — samples, loops, and stems. Browsing thousands of assets had to feel as good as hearing them.

sections.title: Listen while you look.
sections.body: Inline previews let producers audition tracks without leaving the grid — the fastest path from search to 'load into the DAW'.

sections.title: Downloads that don't break the flow.
sections.body: Cart, licensing, and instant delivery are reduced to a few uncluttered steps. The store stays out of the way of the music.

sections.title: Studio-grade aesthetics.
sections.body: Deep tones, waveform motifs, and precise typography create a brand that producers trust at first glance.

overview.title: Retail that converts.
overview.body: El-Imperia is a full retail e-commerce operation. The store needed merchandising power, effortless checkout, and a presence that sells.

sections.title: Grids that merchandise.
sections.body: Product photography, filters, and category storytelling are layered into a tight grid — shoppers find what they want, then discover what they didn't.

sections.title: The shortest path to paid.
sections.body: Cart → address → payment in three calm steps. Every input is engineered to reduce abandonment at the exact moment it matters.

sections.title: Premium shelf presence.
sections.body: A composed palette and editorial product pages give the store the confidence of a flagship, not a marketplace stall.

choo_choo_world.name: GardenHouse Eco-Resort
choo_choo_world.tags: hospitality • garden hotel concept • booking • web

overview.title: A room in the garden.
overview.body: GardenHouse is an eco-resort where architecture dissolves into landscape. The site had to make visitors feel the soil, the light, and the silence.

sections.title: Nature as interface.
sections.body: Soft greens, organic shapes, and slow scroll rhythm mirror the resort itself — every interaction quieter than the last.

sections.title: Choose the sky you wake under.
sections.body: Cabin galleries, garden suites, and glamping pitches are presented as distinct micro-worlds, each with its own mood and view.

sections.title: Reserve the seasons.
sections.body: Availability, rates, and seasonal packages fold into one gentle flow — booking feels like planning a retreat, not a transaction.

soda_experience.name: BiMark Exchange
soda_experience.tags: virtual assets • marketplace • digital goods • platform

overview.title: Digital goods, liquid market.
overview.body: BiMark is a marketplace for virtual assets — accounts, keys, and digital inventory. Buyers needed trust; sellers needed reach.

sections.title: Listings that move.
sections.body: Categorized listings with live status, price history, and seller reputation make the market feel alive — and the next deal one glance away.

sections.title: Escrow as a feature.
sections.body: Guaranteed transactions are surfaced throughout the flow — badges, timelines, and protections turn a risky category into a safe one.

sections.title: Marketplace speed.
sections.body: Instant search, snappy filters, and responsive controls across devices keep traders in motion. The interface stays light; the market stays deep.

faq.q1: How much does a website cost to build in Cyprus from scratch?
faq.a1: Cost follows the type and the difficulty of the work. We set the figure after the brief is written. A one-page site with us starts from 800€, a corporate site from 1200€, an online store from 1900€. A template site is possible: from 300€, usually live in 3–5 days. It costs less to start and more to keep — and it is harder to reach the top of search.
faq.a2: We recommend our own. It is simple, fast, and cut to each client. It runs 3–5 times faster than common commercial CMS tools, stays stable, stays secure, and handles real multilingual work — with lower cost to build and to keep.
faq.q3: Will we be able to update the site ourselves?
faq.a3: Yes. The CMS is clear and spare — no extra fields, a visual editor for text, tables, images, and links. For stores we add import and export from your own documents. One action updates prices, photos, and details.
faq.q4: Does a ready-made design make the site cheaper?
faq.a4: Yes — the first invoice is lower. Support and later modules usually cost more. If you do not plan to grow the site, add material, or push it in search, a template can be the right cut. There is a middle path: you choose a layout from a catalog; we finish it for your brief, then build a unique responsive front and the code behind it.
faq.q5: Do you build websites for free?
faq.a5: We do not recommend free builders. Most are paid after a short trial. The monthly fee is often higher than good hosting, and the result is slower and weaker. Search rarely lifts builder sites. You save a little now, pay more later, and cannot move the code. The time is lost.
faq.q6: How do we get a site without wasting money?
faq.a6: We attend to each client. If you are starting out, we can set a leaner path — without lowering the standard of the work.
faq.a7: Yes, we can. In practice, the strongest text comes from you. A studio writer is not inside your trade; they can only summarise what the web already holds. To outrank rivals, the words must be yours. The sound method is shared work: your people write the substance or the structure; we shape the language, the keys, and the placement.
faq.q8: What else do you take on?
faq.a8: We take the work as a whole: domain, its history, a full reading of rivals, an interface that brings the right requests, tests at every stage, and checks on the devices your clients actually use.
